snippets.text: The second essential feature of stroke is its focal signature. The neurologic deficit reflects both the location and the size of the infarct or hemorrhage. Hemiplegia stands as the most typical sign of stroke, whether in the cerebral hemisphere or brainstem, but there are many other manifestations, occurring in recognizable combinations. These include paralysis, numbness, and sensory deficits of many types on one side of the body, aphasia, visual field defects, diplopia, dizziness, dysarthria, and so forth. The neurovascular syndromes enable the physician to localize the lesion—sometimes so precisely that even the affected arterial branch can be specified—and to indicate whether the lesion is an infarct or a hemorrhage. These syndromes are described in the sections that follow. This group of diseases has also provided the most instructive approach to localization in neurology. As our colleague C.M.
